event.name: Film Tottenham presents Rebel Party
event.summary: Supported by Film Hub London, managed by Film London. Proud to be a partner of the BFI Film Audience Network, funded by the National Lottery

modules.text:
Film Tottenham presents Rebel Party!

The Beehive Pub, Tottenham, 30th August to 25th October

With support from Film London, the BFI Film Audience Network and the National Lottery, Film Tottenham aim to build on their community cinema programme bringing Rebellion and Party to the Beehive pub with vibrant imagery and characters that ignite! Starting in August, and part of Rip It Up, a major BFI and Film Audience Network UK-wide season the programme will include Quadrophenia, Twin Town, Young Soul Rebels, Human Traffic, Trainspotting, It’s All Gone Pete Tong, This Is England and Kneecap.

There will be post film discussions and some screenings will have special guests including Kneecap Producer Jack Tarling, artist Reggiimental, indie filmmaker Gary Thomas and documentary filmmaker Alessandro Ugo.

We will be screening the films on a projector screen in the Beehive and aim to show each film with subtitles.


Early bird tickets are out now!

Here is the line up! A synopsis for each film is further below.

Sunday 30th August: 6.30pm - Quadrophenia (1979) with post film discussion

Sunday 6th September: 6.30pm - Human Traffic (1999) plus a Q and A with documentary filmmaker Alessandro Ugo discussing his time documenting the "Tekno" and "Free Party" music scene

Sunday 13th September: 6.30pm - This Is England (2006) with post film discussion

Sunday 20th September: 6.30pm - Kneecap (2024) plus a Q and A with Kneecap producer Jack Tarling discussing the making of the film and its themes

Sunday 27th September: 6.30pm - It's All Gone Pete Tong (2004) plus a Q and A with indie writer/director Gary Thomas discussing his relationship with sound and music as a partially deaf filmmaker

Saturday 3rd October: 6.30pm - Trainspotting (1996) with post film discussion

Friday 9th October: 6.30pm - Twin Town (1997) with post film discussion

Sunday 25th October: 6.30pm - Young Soul Rebels (1991) plus a performance and Q and A with artist Reggiimental discussing his time working with prison radio, his own music production and how music can inspire hope and rebellion


Join us at The Beehive Pub, Tottenham. We are in the function room behind the main bar.

Screening venue: The Beehive Pub, Stoneleigh Road, London N17 9JW


Our screenings are for 18+ only.

Maximum of 2 tickets per purchase.

Film Tottenham is a creative hub for filmmakers and film in Tottenham.

You can follow us on Instagram and Facebook @filmtottenham

Film Tottenham is run by We are Corporate Ltd

Refunds policy: We are a small indie but can issue refunds up to 7 days before a film screening. We unfortunately cannot refund eventbrite fees.

We take imagery of our events to document them for marketing (and because we're proud). For funding reasons, our event photos will be sent to BFI and Film London for their marketing and press/evaluation purposes. If you do not wish to be in any imagery please just let us know on the day.


Here are the synopsis for each film! We hope you enjoy the line up!


Quadrophenia (1979)


Director: Franc Roddam

Cast: Phil Daniels, Ray Winstone, Timothy Spall, Sting, Leslie Ash

Running Time: 120 mins

Jimmy is a young Mod looking for pills, thrills and a sense of identity in 60s London. His increasing reliance on the buzz provided by the gang mentality of his friends reaches its height in the Brighton Bank Holiday confrontations with the Rockers. An inevitable comedown follows when he is expected to return to the plodding banality of everyday life.

Distributor: Universal Pictures

Rating: 15


Human Traffic (1999)


Director: Justin Kerrigan

Cast: John Simm, Danny Dyer, Lorraine Pilkington, Shaun Parkes, Nicola Reynolds

Running Time: 99 mins

Looking for an escape from boring 9-5 jobs, bad relationships, and dysfunctional families, five Cardiff friends plan a night out to remember, where all that exists is clubs, drugs, pubs and parties. Journey with them through the highs and lows of the weekend, substance-induced and otherwise, for wild escapades and unexpected epiphanies.

This cult classic of the ‘Cool Cymru’ era boasts Danny Dyer in a full-on feature debut. Human Traffic is an unapologetic celebration of 90s club culture and youthful hedonism with an unparallelled soundtrack, featuring Matthew Herbert, Fatboy Slim, Brainbug and Orbital. The weekend has landed.

Distributor: Universal Pictures

Rating: 15


This Is England (2006)


Director: Shane Meadows

Cast: Stephen Graham, Jo Hartley, Thomas Turgoose, Vicky McClure, Jack O'Connell

Running Time: 100 mins

This Is England, is the story of a summertime school holiday, those long weeks between terms where life changing events can take place. It’s 1983 and school is out. 12-year-old Shaun (Thomas Turgoose) is an isolated lad growing up in a grim coastal town, whose father has died fighting in the Falklands war. Over the course of the summer holiday he finds fresh male role models when those in the local skinhead scene take him in. With his new friends Shaun discovers a world of parties, first love and the joys of Dr Martin boots. Here he also meets Combo (Stephen Graham), an older, racist skinhead who has recently got out of prison. As Combo’s gang harass the local ethnic minorities, the course is set for a rite of passage that will hurl Shaun from innocence to experience.

Distributor: StudioCanal

Rating: 18


Kneecap (2024)


Director: Rich Peppiatt

Cast: Móglaí Bap, Mo Chara, DJ Próvaí, and Michael Fassbender

Running Time: 105 mins

Of the 80,000 native Irish speakers, 6,000 live in the North of Ireland and three of them became a rap group called Kneecap. This is the real-life story of how this anarchic Belfast trio became the unlikely figureheads of a civil rights movement to save and reinvigorate their mother tongue.

Distributor: Curzon

Rating: 18


It's All Gone Pete Tong (2004)


Director: Michael Dowse

Cast: Paul Kaye, Beatriz Batarda, Kate Magowan, Mike Wilmot

Running Time: 90 mins

The legend of Frankie Wilde. The deaf DJ. lt's All Gone Pete Tong is a hysterically funny comedy following the tragic life of the legendary DJ Frankie Wilde from international fame through to his subsequent battle with adversity. Frankie is living the opulent life of a superstar, residing in his trophy villa in Ibiza with his trophy wife. But then tragedy hits, as his career and his well-being are suddenly threatened by a seemingly insurmountable twist of fate. This feel good comedy has something for everybody.

Distributor: Lionsgate

Rating: 15


Trainspotting (1996)


Director: Danny Boyle

Cast: Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Kevin McKidd, Robert Carlyle, Kelly Macdonald

Running Time: 93 mins

Smart, funny, sickly and sometimes just plain unconscious, MARK RENTON is a hero for our times. Set in an underbelly of Edinburgh the city fathers never dreamed of, TRAINSPOTTING is the story of MARK and his so-called friends - a bunch of losers, liars, psychos, thieves and junkies. Hilarious but harrowing, the film charts the disintegration of their friendship as they proceed, seemingly inevitably, towards self destruction. Mark alone has the insight and opportunity to escape his fate - but then again, does he really want to “choose life”?

Distributor: Park Circus

Rating: 18


Twin Town (1997)


Director: Kevin Allen

Cast: Rhys Ifans, Llyr Ifans, Dougray Scott

Running Time: 99 mins

The serene setting of Swansea is suddenly cleaved apart by two young lads tearing through the neighbourhood in a two tone BMW 525. Their dysfunctional family scrapes together a living from their dole money and odd-jobs offered to their father.

Distributor: Universal Pictures

Rating: 18


Young Soul Rebels (1991)


Director: Isaac Julien

Cast: Valentine Nonyela, Mo Sesay, Dorian Healy, Sophie Okonedo

Running Time: 100 mins

A convincing picture of late 70s London, youth culture meets identity politics in this part-thriller, part-gay love story set days before the Queen's Silver Jubilee celebrations. The hedonistic world of pirate DJs Chris and Caz is shattered when a close friend is killed while cruising in the local park. The black community suspect the National Front, but the police have other ideas.

Distributor: Universal Pictures

Rating: 18
